parts:
Hi, Henrik.
Thank you for all your kind help. I see now that for some reason my Windows
XP Pro Explorer hides the lnk extension, even though I have all folders set
to show extensions. I don't know why the behavior on your and my computer
is dissimilar in this respect. Perhaps it's because I'm in "Classic" mode.
All is clear when viewing dir contents from the command line though. I had
never realized that shortcuts have the lnk extension, so sorry about not
getting this earlier. I do have a suggestion, however, that the
instructions be modified slightly to avoid confusing others who can't see
the lnk extension.

Anyway, I read in all the affy exon files, and I'm back on track. Thanks
again. kv

The file should be named "HuEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf.lnk", but the file is
named "HuEx-1_0-st-v1.cdf.lnk.lnk" according to your output, i.e. you
should add the ".cdf" part, not the ".lnk" part. When I create a
shortcut on my WinXP from a file named "Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf" the link
file is named "Mapping250K_Nsp.lnk". In order for the package no
recognize this as a CDF file, it has to be renamed to
"Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf.lnk".

-rwx------ 1 hb mkpasswd 194455495 Jun 6 2006 Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf

The "FooBar.cdf.lnk" file links to the "Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf" file.

Hi,

true, it turns out that the Windows Explorer hides some filenames
extension (almost) no matter what. I've updated the docs "Setting up
annotation files" explaining this.

Cheers

Henrik
